relations.subject: backup:backup-task
relations.evidence: For any given repository, the Backup Service performs one task at a time, with each task maintaining a lock on the repository.

relations.subject: backup:merge-task
relations.evidence: Merges are supported for filesystem-based repositories: however, merges are _not_ supported for cloud-based repositories.

relations.subject: backup:repository-pause
relations.evidence: Once a pause is executed by the administrator, no scheduled task for the repository is executed.

relations.subject: backup:repository-deletion
relations.evidence: Repositories can be deleted. However, no repository can be deleted until it has been archived, as described above, in [Archive Repositories](#archive-repositories).

relations.subject: n1ql:build-index
relations.evidence: When restoring Vector Indexes, you must run the BUILD INDEX command only after the Key-Value Data restoration is complete.

relations.subject: backup:restore-operation
relations.evidence:
Map Data

Lets you have the restore task restore a backed-up bucket's data to a different bucket.

relations.subject: backup:restore-operation
relations.evidence: Lets you enter a regular expression the restore task uses to filter the key values. The restore task only restores a document if its key matches the regular expression.

relations.subject: backup:restore-operation
relations.evidence: These fields let you choose how the restore task handles time to live (TTL) values in the documents it's restoring.

relations.subject: backup:restore-operation
relations.evidence: By default, the restore task does not overwrite an existing document that has a more recent modification time than its backed up version. Select **Force Updates** to have the restore task always overwrite existing documents with the version in the backup even if the existing document is more recent.

relations.subject: backup:restore-operation
relations.evidence: When checked, the restore task drops scopes and collections that currently exist in buckets but had been dropped prior to the backup's creation.

relations.subject: backup:restore-operation
relations.evidence: By default, the restore task exits with an error message if a bucket being restored from the backup does not currently exist in the cluster. Selecting **Auto-create Buckets** has the restore task create any missing buckets.

notable_absence.finding: This page states only that 'the Full Admin role must have been assigned' for use of the Backup Service, and never mentions the narrower role:backup-admin ('Backup Full Admin') the REST reference documents as gating the Backup Service's own admin endpoints (per that concept's registry note). A reader of this UI-only page would not learn that a narrower role than Full Admin exists for Backup Service access at all.

cross_component_finding: The Restore dialog's Cluster field instruction reads 'Include the REST API port—​by default, 8091 for unencrypted HTTP and 18901 for secure HTTPS connections' - '18901' does not match the registry's promoted port:18091 (the TLS Web Console/Cluster Manager REST port established from other pages in this corpus), and looks like a transposition typo in the source page itself rather than a genuinely different port; flagged here rather than minted as a new port concept or silently corrected. Separately, the Repositories view's three panels (Active/Imported/Archived, 'Currently, all panels are blank') visually corroborate, from the UI-procedure angle, the three-way repository lifecycle (active/archived/imported) round 25 established purely from REST evidence - independent confirmation that the UI exposes the identical repository/plan/task vocabulary rather than a simplified framing of it, exactly as this round's hypothesis anticipated checking for.
